contract_revision_note: v2 comparison set, 2026-07-30. All three targets now satisfy CONTRACT-v2 section 3 (terminal outcome in the POST body), so end-to-end saga duration is measured identically and order_create_latency_ms is comparison-eligible - earned by target changes, not relabelling. Protocol is h1 on every stack because k6 cannot drive h2c (driver limit, verified against curl and h2load; the targets do serve h2c). Restate stays baseline-only; spring-on-exeris stays exploratory (still polled).

compatible_targets.notes: Comparison-eligible within-tier h1 loopback under required_contract=exeris_community_h1_v2. Runs the saga in-process; flow state persists to Postgres, so part of its Postgres cost is saga state (see deployment-footprint.json).
compatible_targets.claim_scope_note: Per-step scope governs. order_create_latency_ms became eligible on 2026-07-30 when every stack was made CONTRACT-v2 section 3 compliant (terminal outcome in the POST body); before that the polled stacks measured a flat ~1010 ms of client poll sleep against ~28 ms inline, an artifact large enough to reverse the apparent ordering. recommend_latency_ms is platform-natural ONLY - the stacks issue different work there (one Cypher query vs 1+N traversals forced by the graph SPI), measured at 2.6x Neo4j CPU for exeris.

compatible_targets.notes: Comparison-eligible within-tier h1 loopback under required_contract=quarkus_axon_neo4j_h1_v2. Runs the ENTIRE saga synchronously on the request thread and returns the terminal outcome inline.

Saga progression is async via a tracking processor tuned to 16 segments (section 9(d) disclosure); the request thread awaits completion (section 9(a) deviation). NOT the same architecture as quarkus-hibernate despite both using Axon.

framework_difference.baseline_event: Exeris Events L3 with transactional outbox
Exeris Events L3 with transactional outbox

framework_difference.shared_event: Both use Axon Event Sourcing + Outbox

forbidden_pairs.reason: Community vs Enterprise cross-tier — protocol fairness requires separate contracts
Cross-protocol comparisons are out of scope (H1 vs H2C vs H3 must be segregated)
Network-path vs loopback transport modes cannot be compared directly
Cross-backend comparisons are invalid (neo4j vs postgres-graph/pgq)
AGE compatibility runs are not performance-equivalent to PGQ pure runs

cross_tier_equivalence_constraints.load_model: EXACTLY constant-arrival-rate, 50 sessions/s measurement (identical across all targets)
cross_tier_equivalence_constraints.concurrency_note: VU counts are a POOL CEILING under an arrival-rate executor, NOT fixed concurrency. Measured peak concurrency ~342. The previous 'EXACTLY 100 VUs / 100 H2C connections' text described a closed-loop model this scenario does not run and was never true of it.
cross_tier_equivalence_constraints.think_time: EXACTLY 800-2500 ms random sleep (identical jitter distribution)
cross_tier_equivalence_constraints.protocol: EXACTLY HTTP/1.1 cleartext on every stack. NOT h2c: k6 cannot drive cleartext HTTP/2 (grafana/k6#970). The targets do serve h2c - verified with curl and h2load - so an h2c track is possible with a different driver and needs its own workload_profile_key.
cross_tier_equivalence_constraints.resolution_model: EXACTLY inline on all three (terminal outcome in the POST body). Any stack resolving by polling is NOT comparable on saga duration.
cross_tier_equivalence_constraints.database: EXACTLY identical: PostgreSQL + Neo4j, same instances, pool ceiling 256 on every stack (measured peak backends 16-37, so the pool is not a limiter for anyone).

acceptable_framework_differences.framework_overhead: Exeris Flow (kernel-built) vs Quarkus/Spring Axon Framework
Exeris Graph L2 (native) vs Neo4j Bolt driver (Community)
acceptable_framework_differences.attribution: Graph driver heap allocation and serialization (expected, documented)

acceptable_framework_differences.framework_overhead: Exeris Events L3 (kernel) vs Axon Event Sourcing + Outbox
acceptable_framework_differences.attribution: Event subscription and outbox polling mechanics (expected, documented)

overclaiming_prevention: ALL comparisons MUST include framework overhead caveats
DO NOT claim 'Exeris is X% faster' without acknowledging Axon Framework is a separate system
CORRECT CLAIM: 'E2E order sagas complete X% faster on Exeris native Flow vs Quarkus/Spring + Axon Framework (framework overhead component: ~Y%)'
Include attribution table: saga orchestration overhead (kernel vs framework) + graph driver overhead + event backend overhead
Distinguish between throughput and saga completion latency (different metrics, different claims)
Use 95% CI ranges for all claims; absolute differences require MIN 15% relative separation

must_include: Protocol equivalence table (identical H2C, no TLS)
Payload equivalence attestation (identical order JSON schema)
Concurrency equivalence table (100 VUs, identical thread pool)
Database equivalence attestation (identical PostgreSQL + Neo4j versions)
Saga completion rate by state (COMPLETED, COMPENSATED, FAILED)
Compensation polling statistics (avg polls, max polls, timeout rate)
known asymmetries for query language/planner differences
resolution model per stack (all three inline as of 2026-07-30)
arrival rate and measured peak concurrency (50/s, ~342)
whole-deployment footprint per component (target JVM + Postgres + Neo4j + Axon Server), not target JVM alone
graph access-pattern caveat wherever recommend_latency_ms appears (1 Cypher query vs 1+N traversals)
must_not_include: Absolute claims like 'X% faster' without framework overhead attribution
Cross-protocol comparisons (H1 vs H2C vs H3)
Saga success rate without compensation state breakdown
backend superiority claims from cross-family runs
unqualified percentage speed claims across mixed graph_backend_family
recommend_latency_ms presented as a runtime-speed comparison (the stacks issue different work there)
target-JVM-only RSS presented as the deployment footprint (Axon Server sits outside it)
any aggregation of these results with runs under the superseded h2c-named contracts

claim_scope_enforcement_gap.finding: scripts/run-comparative.sh claim_scope_for_target() recognises only the literal strings comparison_eligible and descriptive_only, so it cannot express the per-step scope above. It will happily pass a recommend_latency_ms comparison that the contracts qualify as platform-natural-only.
claim_scope_enforcement_gap.consequence: A strict-gate PASS attests protocol/payload/concurrency fairness. It does NOT attest that every per-step metric is comparable. recommend_latency_ms must carry the graph-SPI caveat in any row that includes it.
claim_scope_enforcement_gap.resolved_since_last_revision: order_create_latency_ms and order_poll_latency_ms are no longer restricted - the section 3 target changes removed the resolution-model asymmetry that made them incomparable.
